version.changelog: Publish the reviewed Suno Lyrics to Song workflow with its English ClawHub listing.

llm.summary: The skill appears to be a real lyrics-to-song workflow, but it bundles broad account authority, spending capability, arbitrary upload support, and silent self-updates that go beyond the narrow song-generation purpose.

dimensions.detail: The skill detects the agent platform, records installation metadata, and can read and upload arbitrary caller-supplied local regular files, which is not necessary for the lyrics-to-song use case.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation and authorization create shared state under ~/.beatra, store a bearer token, register the package with Beatra, and request a full shared Beatra device authorization rather than a narrow music-only grant.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives careful instructions for one paid generation after a production card, but it also exposes a generic MCP call path and upload command that are broader than the documented lyrics-to-song workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The bundled client silently checks for and installs package updates by default, and the uninstall script can revoke and remove shared Beatra credential state when it decides this is the last Beatra skill.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core Suno lyrics-to-song flow is coherent and user-directed, but the bundled Beatra client and authorization request cover unrelated media tools, artifact access, task control, uploads, and wallet spending.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Install only if you trust Beatra with a shared device token that can spend credits and access multiple Beatra media/task capabilities, not just Suno music generation. Consider disabling silent updates with the documented update --auto off command, and be cautious about invoking upload or uninstall commands because they affect local files or shared Beatra connection state.
llm.findings:
[LP3] unexpected: Network access and a credential are expected for paid music generation, but the documented and coded authority is much broader than a music-only lyrics workflow.
[TP4] unexpected: The advertised creative workflow is coherent, yet OAuth, telemetry, self-update, upload, and generic MCP tool execution materially exceed what a user would expect from the title alone.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Silent automatic package replacement is disclosed and includes integrity checks, but default self-modification during ordinary use is not required for song generation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The self-update implementation downloads manifests and archives and replaces local package files; safeguards are present, but the capability expands the trust boundary.
[SDI-2] unexpected: First-use installation registration sends package, version, platform, and installation reference metadata to Beatra; it is disclosed and best-effort, but not core to lyrics transformation.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The authorization helper requests broad scopes including image, video, speech, voices, artifacts, task control, and wallet spending, not just music generation.
[SDI-2] expected: Wallet spending is plausibly needed for paid generation, but combining it with unrelated scopes increases account blast radius.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The upload command can read and upload an arbitrary local regular file chosen by path, while the lyrics-to-song workflow does not need local file upload.
[SQP-2] expected: The production card states approval starts one paid generation, so the paid call is user-directed, though users should understand that the approval is the spend confirmation.
[PE3] expected: Credential access occurs in the uninstall/revocation flow, not as theft, but it still gives the package lifecycle code direct control over shared Beatra credentials.
[RA1] unexpected: The explicit update command and default auto-update path are maintenance features, not part of the creative workflow, and enable package self-modification.
